blk_part_02_part_2_why_the_building_stop.text: First, the city had other needs. In 1474, the craftsmen were needed to make the city's defences stronger against the Duke of Burgundy. A city under threat cares more about walls than towers. Second, the money began to disappear. By 1473, income from pilgrims had fallen. Later, the Reformation and wars made things worse. The cathedral lost its money from indulgences, which were special payments collected by the Church. Major work stopped in 1473 or 1474, and construction ended completely around 1560.
